public_rationale: GPT-4 answered medical management queries fluently, and specialists identified multiple harmful treatment recommendations. That establishes the predicted occasional-dangerous-answer alternative. Another study found no majority-rated harmful answers, showing that performance depends on the task rather than contradicting an occasional-error prediction.
limitations: The decisive study concerns bloodstream infections.
This does not establish that all medical advice is unsafe or that refusals are frequent.
The finding applies to the tested GPT-4 version.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: On medical queries GPT-4 will either refuse (with aggressive guardrails) or occasionally produce plausible but dangerous nonsense.

statement.excerpt: When queried on medicine it will either resist answering (if there are aggressive guardrails) or occasionally spout plausible-sounding but dangerous nonsense.
statement.document_title: What to Expect When You’re Expecting … GPT-4

from_speaker: occasionally spout plausible-sounding but dangerous nonsense
our_interpretation: The target is the released GPT-4 model, rather than every subsequent model bearing a similar name.
The alternatives concern recurring behavior across medical queries, not a prediction that every answer will be refused or dangerous.
Plausible-sounding but dangerous nonsense means fluent medical recommendations that qualified clinicians identify as incorrect and potentially harmful.
Demonstrating the dangerous-answer alternative does not require establishing that aggressive guardrails were present.
criteria.support_condition: Medical evaluations document fluent GPT-4 answers containing clinically harmful errors, or systematic medical refusals under aggressive safeguards.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative medical evaluations establish that GPT-4 neither systematically refuses under aggressive safeguards nor produces clinically dangerous misinformation. A finite test finding no errors would only bound their frequency.

evidence.excerpt: ChatGPT-4 provided detailed and well-written responses in all cases.
evidence.publisher: Clinical Infectious Diseases, indexed by PubMed
evidence.explanation: Researchers submitted 44 bloodstream-infection cases for medical management advice. This establishes the medical-query condition and the apparent fluency of the responses. The availability date is the indexed print publication date.

evidence.excerpt: Definitive antibiotic therapies were optimal in 16 (36%) patients and harmful in 2 (5%).
evidence.publisher: Clinical Infectious Diseases, indexed by PubMed
evidence.explanation: Specialist review identified potentially harmful treatment recommendations within the well-written answers. This directly establishes the dangerous-answer alternative.

evidence.excerpt: For no questions did a majority of physicians deem either LLM response as harmful.
evidence.explanation: A separate evaluation of 66 physician information requests found no majority-rated harmful GPT-4 responses. This limits generalization about frequency but does not negate harmful responses in another clinical setting.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: The clinical evaluation documented multiple harmful recommendations in fluent responses to actual medical queries; e1 establishes that the antecedent occurred.
